    - heading "Understand Bearings" [level=2]
    - paragraph: "A bearing is a direction angle measured clockwise from north. In Bearings, that statement is the exact rule used on the labelled chart and in the three numerical examples. A useful rule is Bearing convention: bearing = clockwise angle from north. You can learn Bearings by trying one small example instead of long theory."
    - paragraph: Start at north. Turn clockwise to the direction line. Write the angle as three digits. Try the example below. Write your steps and choose an answer before opening the comparison.
    - paragraph: "In real life, navigation: Ships use bearings. Watch out: Measuring bearing from east like a standard graph angle. Bearings start from north and turn clockwise."
